headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared filesystem/MCP plus broad egress; no critical compliance issue is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while gpt-researcher reads files and calls MCP/APIs. That creates a default pathway where content from one agent can be consumed by the other as trusted input. The pair is not documented as isolated, so injection risk is plausible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF Continue writes attacker-controlled text into shared workspace files and gpt-researcher ingests those files as prompts or context, injection is possible.
IF either agent forwards raw MCP output into the other without provenance checks, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents.
Require provenance tags on all file-derived content before prompting either agent.
Route inter-agent handoff through a human-reviewed summary only.
Turn off MCP for one agent during cross-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, editor buffers, and workspace files; gpt-researcher reads local documents and uploads content to external APIs such as OpenAI/Tavily/Google Gemini. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or documents can flow from Continue into gpt-researcher and then out to third parties by default unless explicitly constrained.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, files opened in Continue can be read by gpt-researcher.
IF gpt-researcher sends those files or derived excerpts to external APIs, the data leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and research tasks.
Block sensitive directories from gpt-researcher input paths.
Prefer local-only models for any shared documents.
Review API-provider settings before running research jobs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate local state through filesystem access and subprocess execution, and Continue explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. Even though Continue does not modify git state, overlapping writes to the same directory can still clobber files or intermediate artifacts when gpt-researcher is running concurrently.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF gpt-researcher and Continue run concurrently on the same task tree, one agent can overwrite artifacts the other expects to remain stable.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes with a simple manual handoff step.
Keep one agent read-only during the other's write phase.
Snapshot the workspace before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional writes for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code-oriented outputs and gpt-researcher is designed to generate research reports and citations. If the research agent treats Continue's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into polished but incorrect reports or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher ingests Continue-generated claims without source checking, incorrect facts can be amplified.
IF either agent is asked to summarize the other's output as ground truth, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require citations for every factual claim before publication.
Insert a manual verification step between agents.
Use Continue only for drafting, not factual assertions.
Have gpt-researcher re-open primary sources before finalizing.
requires-engineering: add automated claim-to-source validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code and editor buffers, while gpt-researcher handles local documents and sends content to third-party APIs. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for sensitive documents or code, even though no specific HIPAA/GDPR certification gap is documented. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential documents are placed into gpt-researcher, third-party API processing may violate local policy.
IF Continue and gpt-researcher are used under different retention expectations, the same data class can be retained inconsistently.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of gpt-researcher jobs.
Use local-only inference for sensitive material.
Confirm retention settings for each API provider.
Separate personal, regulated, and public workspaces.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared data-handling policy.
